extraction.name: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models
extraction.description: Paper introducing the pointer sentinel mixture architecture for neural sequence models and the WikiText language modeling dataset.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The WikiText dataset was constructed by selecting Wikipedia articles that fit the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API, then sections primarily featuring lists were removed, minor HTML bugs were removed, mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with special tokens, and normalization/tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer with additional fixes. Words with counts below 3 were discarded and out-of-vocabulary words were mapped to a special token.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles selected from Good and Featured articles; Penn Treebank is also used for language modeling experiments, but the new dataset is extracted from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Removed list-heavy sections by default; removed sort keys and Edit buttons leaked from HTML; replaced mathematical formulae and LaTeX code with special tokens; normalized and tokenized text with Moses tokenizer augmented to split numbers and apply minor fixes; discarded words with frequency below 3 and mapped out-of-vocabulary words to a special token.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted raw Wikipedia text from markup, removed unwanted sections and artifacts, normalized and tokenized the text, built a vocabulary by discarding low-frequency words, and replaced out-of-vocabulary words with a special token.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Wikipedia articles were selected based on Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors; these articles had been reviewed by humans and considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the WikiText dataset is freely available and will be made available to the community; no explicit versioning, maintenance schedule, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes limitations of Penn Treebank including lowercasing, removal of punctuation, and a restricted 10k vocabulary, which make it unrealistic for real language use and problematic for rare words and named entities. It also notes that some larger language modeling datasets have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Penn Treebank is limited by lowercasing, stripped punctuation, and a 10k vocabulary, which reduces realism and harms rare-word modeling. The paper also notes that some alternative datasets have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering. WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 are designed for language modeling and longer dependencies, but no explicit non-recommended uses are stated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling benchmark for training, validation, and testing; used to evaluate models on long-range dependencies and rare words. The paper presents WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 as benchmark datasets for language modeling.
